editorial.headline: Silkworm Cocoons Are Nationally Open, but Bali Blocks PMA Registration
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers silkworm cultivation and breeding for cocoons, with all business scales open nationally but PMA registration blocked in Bali under the moratorium.
editorial.body:
Silkworm cultivation is a narrow, physical activity in this record: the breeding and raising of silkworms to produce cocoons. The Indonesian scope is not written as a broad textile, trading, or processing category. Its centre of gravity is the biological production stage, where the business activity is the cultivation and breeding of the worm itself and the output is the cocoon or pupal casing. For founders, that distinction matters because the code describes the activity being registered, not a romantic idea of the silk industry around it.

Nationally, the record is straightforward. The PMA status is **TERBUKA**, and the foreign-ownership ceiling is **100%**. The scale field is equally broad: **Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, Besar** are all open. Read plainly, that means this activity is not reserved only for a single size of operator in the national record, and it is not capped below full foreign ownership under the PMA ceiling shown here. A small silkworm-breeding operation and a larger cultivation setup both sit inside the listed scale range, as long as the registered activity remains the cultivation and breeding of silkworms for cocoons.

The Bali position is the harder part, and it should be read without smoothing it over. Even though the national PMA status is open, the record marks Bali as **BLOCCATO_CLASSE_RISCHIO** and sets **l4_bali_blocked** to true. The reason given is specific: OSS risk at scale **Besar** is **Rendah/Menengah-Rendah** on every scope, and that places it inside the Bali moratorium dated May 13, 2026. The moratorium rule in the record is island-wide and permanent: Bali province blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA. So the honest lede is simple: a foreigner cannot register this activity as PMA in Bali today, even though the same activity is nationally foreign-open.

That tension is the practical editorial point of this code. On paper, the activity is accessible across all listed business scales and allows full foreign ownership under the cited national framework, **Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021**. In Bali, however, the provincial filter overrides the practical outcome for PMA registration because the activity falls into the blocked risk class under the moratorium source, **Gubernur letter B.27.000/642/PM/DPMPTSP**. This is not a warning about permits, capital, taxes, or timing beyond what the record says. It is a registration reality: nationally open does not mean Bali-open when the local moratorium blocks the risk class.
